content.title: Message from Dr Alex Awiti, Interim Dean, GSMC on Covid-19
content.summary: Once the pandemic is over, I am confident GSMC will emerge stronger. We have learnt a lot of things during this process.

media.alt: Message from Dr Alex Awiti, Interim Dean, GSMC on Covid-19

content.text: How is GSMC managing operations during this tough time?

It has been a steep learning curve. GSMC has had to readjust and recalibrate its programmes. We have gone into different modes of re-planning and we now have different schedules for our colleagues who are supporting our operations. We have a weekly schedule to ensure that we are not all at the office at the same time, in line with the government directives of social distancing. Our faculty have worked really hard over the past weeks to mount all our programmes to an online deliverable model and continue teaching virtually. We have moved all our operations to near normalcy and we are operating at about 85 percent operational capacity and efficiency.
What is your encouragement to the staff as they work through these uncertain times?

What we are experiencing is not normal. I know it's challenging because we are intruding into family space, as you have to take your meetings in your homes. However, your presence at home signals that you are available for your children, spouse, partner, pet and others who live with you  to come and talk to you, and yet you want to maintain your standard operating work routine. I would encourage you to try work-life balance and integration. You need to figure out how to work well, stay healthy and be available to your families.

This is extremely challenging and we have all been cultured in an education environment where we have the lecturer in front of us. We are used to sitting next to our colleagues, making eye contact, feeling the presence and the creative and intellectual energy in one space. Unfortunately, that is absent now. We have to learn virtually and it is difficult to maintain the engagement and intellectual conversation contact in the course of the lectures. I thank you for scheduling the time and the continual personal sacrifices to ensure that you attend the classes virtually. Stand strong and firm. This is not going to go on forever. We look forward to welcoming you back to GSMC and you can be sure that when you are back, we will appreciate you more as we understand that face-to-face delivery does not have an appropriate substitute.
Any tips/hacks on working from home?

Yes. Don't break your house or convert it fully into an office. Don't be mean to your children, spouses, partners, pets and others who live with you. If you are in the middle of a meeting and your child wants to talk to you, respectfully excuse yourself to attend to your child. I have been in meetings where colleagues at the beginning of the meeting have introduced their family members, who have proceeded to say hello. I would encourage this as we are the ones who have invaded your family space. We are trying to make your homes your offices and this will not be easy. Feel free to take breaks as often as you need. Make sure you have a comfortable place to where you can sit and work. Also ensure you attend to the family members who need you. This should work for you and your family too. We don't want to create heartaches and difficulty especially for children who see their parents but cannot talk or feel them.

Use the resources available as much as you can. Reach out to your colleagues, create chat groups and use online forums to work together in a collegial and collaborative way. I know it can be lonely but we are only a phone call, text and chat away. Use this time to do the things that you have wanted to do eg. learn a new skill. Stay connected with your colleagues and make sure you do not break the bonds you have forged and the intellectual connections.
Moving forward: what is your hope for the entity once this pandemic is over?

Once the pandemic is over, I am confident GSMC will emerge stronger. We have learnt a lot of things during this process. In many ways I think the learnings we have garnered from this will support us moving forward in a stronger and determined way. This is not the last major disruption to learning. I am very optimistic and glad that we have not wasted time. We migrated promptly to an online delivery of our programmes and that kind of agility and adaptive resilience will help us in the years to come.
